newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb kills three, wounds 13 in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills three, wounds 13 in Algeria.

text.p: A bomb killed at least three people and wounded 13, two seriously, in the northeastern Algerian town of Lakhdaria on Monday night, Algerian security forces said on Tuesday.

The bomb went off just hours after President Liamine Zeroual told Algeria's 29 million people in a nationwide broadcast that a referendum would be held on November 28, a vote that would seal Algeria's unity.

The attack in Lakhdaria, 55 km (35 miles) from the capital Algiers, came only three days after a bomb in another town killed at least 10 people and wounded more than 70. That bomb, in Kolea, exploded in the heart of a crowded market just before mass Friday prayers.
Authorities blame the attacks on Moslem fundamentalists trying to topple the government.
The security forces, in a statement on the official news agency APS, said the toll from the latest attack was provisional.

Early on Tuesday, Moslem gunmen killed the manager of Algeria's mass-circulation Echourouk newspaper as he left his home in Jolie-Vue suburb, overlooking the fundamentalist bastion of Kouba on the heights of Algiers.

He was the third staff member of the Arabic-language weekly to have been killed in the past three years. The other two were journalists, part of the toll of more than 60 media employees to have been slain.
Moslem guerrillas see media staff, who are subject to harsh censorship on security issues, as supporting the authorities whom the fundamentalists have been trying to topple for five years.
At least 50,000 people have been killed since violence erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
